agents.name: Tivozanib
agents.type: Targeted therapy: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Tivozanib blocks VEGFR signals involved in growing blood vessels. This reduces the support available to the tumour. Effects on healthy blood vessels explain why blood pressure, bleeding, wounds and urine protein need monitoring.
agents.explanation: Tivozanib blocks VEGFR signals involved in growing blood vessels. This reduces the support available to the tumour. Effects on healthy blood vessels explain why blood pressure, bleeding, wounds and urine protein need monitoring.
risks: High blood pressure, occasionally severe; heart failure, heart attack, stroke or clots
Voice changes, tiredness, reduced appetite and weight loss
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, sore mouth and abdominal pain
Painful palms and soles, rash or other skin changes
Thyroid or liver changes, protein in urine and occasionally nephrotic syndrome
Bleeding, including serious bleeding; rare bowel perforation or fistula
Abnormal heart rhythm related to QT prolongation; electrolyte changes
Delayed wound healing; rare brain swelling syndrome (PRES)
agents.watch: Keep a dated dosing calendar and blood-pressure record if requested. Contact the team for persistent diarrhoea, reduced intake, severe tiredness or painful palms/soles. Tell the team before surgery; restart after a break for surgery requires a healing review.

anatomy: Voice changes and tiredness can occur. Severe headache, confusion, seizures or sight changes need urgent assessment.
Soreness, nausea or taste changes may limit eating. Report symptoms early and ask for nutrition support.
Check pressure as advised. Chest pain, fainting, palpitations or sudden breathlessness needs urgent advice.
Blood tests check liver function and electrolytes. Report yellow eyes, dark urine or marked weakness.
Diarrhoea and vomiting can dehydrate you. Severe abdominal pain, black stools or blood in vomit is urgent.
Urine protein can increase. Report swelling, foamy urine or passing much less urine.
Painful red or peeling palms/soles need early treatment. Report pain that limits walking or daily tasks.
Report unusual bleeding, a painful swollen leg or an unhealed wound. Agree any surgery-related treatment break.

support.title: Fertility and contraception
support.text: Discuss fertility and avoid pregnancy. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month afterwards; hormonal contraception should be combined with a barrier method. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree the post-treatment interval with the team.

support.title: Your wider treatment
support.text: Treatment options depend on previous medicines, cancer behaviour, general health and your priorities. Surgery or focused radiotherapy may be appropriate for selected problems; they do not replace this systemic medicine automatically.

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: TIVO-1 compared tivozanib with sorafenib in 517 patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma and no prior VEGF/mTOR-targeted therapy. Median progression-free survival was 11.9 versus 9.1 months (hazard ratio 0.797; 95% confidence interval 0.639–0.993). This supports delayed progression in that population; it does not establish an overall-survival advantage or compare modern immunotherapy combinations.

items.title: Fertility and contraception
items.text: Discuss fertility and avoid pregnancy. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month afterwards; hormonal contraception should be combined with a barrier method. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree the post-treatment interval with the team.

items.title: Your priorities
items.text: Discuss benefit, burden, alternatives including supportive care, and choosing to decline or stop treatment. Trial averages cannot predict your own outcome.
